label: August 1885
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1885 from our dossiers, our first month from the 1880s, placed on 1910 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 32 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1885, our first month from the 1880s. They come from the 44 events in the August 1885 table, which includes July events first reported in August. We did not write dossiers for 17 events with non-Black victims, for duplicates, or for events plainly out of scope. Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Fifteen of the 47 dossiers are set aside. Four are duplicates folded into another record: the Ross and Prewitt shootings at Canton, Texas; one of the two Waterloo reports; and the Gorin warning in Humphreys County. Eleven are out of scope. In five, no report gives the victim's race: Huffman, Fowler, Diana Brown, Halbrook, Addie King. Two were routine arrests (Gus Johnson, John Hunt), one was a two-sided fight (Archie Green), and the Asbury Park color-line campaign involved no force. The hanging of Albert Lee at Milton was reported as by and of Black people, and the posse hunt for John Jones near Lynchburg harmed no one.

Attacks by one person: our definition covers violence by groups and by people acting with public authority, so an attack by a single private person is normally left out. A later check of every August article for such attacks added one dossier: the killing of Charlie, a Black farmhand at Kissimmee, Florida, by W. A. Patterson, who said Charlie had tried to outrage his sister; a justice’s jury found it justifiable. The entry says the attacker acted alone. Whether such cases belong in the count is still open.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched Black and white papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. Black-press clippings are shown as page images and white-press articles as text. For 1885 the Black press is thin: the main Black paper is the New York Freeman, which is still counted under the white press in our sources (LoC pages).

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
